newsitem.title: SWEDEN: P&U says unconcerned about drug side effect.
newsitem.headline: P&U says unconcerned about drug side effect.

text.p: Swedish/U.S. drugs company Pharmacia & Upjohn said it is not worried about about the side effects noted for incontinence agent tolterodin, the company's head of research Goran Ando said on Thursday.
"The side effects do not worry us as few patients have chosen to end treatment or reduce the dose," Ando told a telephone conference.
"We have had a significant demand from patients who want to continue treatment."
Ando said eight to ten percent of patients in the clinical study choose to end treatment compared with seven percent for placebo.
But on the other hand, 27 percent choose to stop using the comparing active agent, the best available alternative, Ando said.
Pharmacia & Upjohn expects to make an application for approval of tolterodin within two months in several countries, for example in the U.S. and Europe.
Ando said it was harder to say when the agent will hit the market.

"After having turned in the applications, it is the authorities that decide when (the drug) is cleared," Ando said. "You could use some kind of 12-15 months rule but it is different in different countries.
"It is impossible to give a timetable, it can go somewhat faster or somewhat slower," he said.
Tolterodine is one of the drugs that analysts see having a large potential.
